analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: G4 Net Bond Supply—Leveling Out
key_insights: GS expects net sovereign bond issuance to stay elevated in 2027 across the G4, but net supply to the public should be stable or lower in the US, Euro Area and UK. Japan is the only major market where net supply to the public is expected to rise modestly.

US: Treasury's reliance on bills, larger buybacks and higher coupon redemptions should cut net coupon supply available to the public from about $1.2tn in 2026 to $1.1tn in 2027. Including bills, net supply to the public is little changed ($1,703bn in 2026 vs $1,700bn in 2027).

GS baseline is that Treasury starts raising auction sizes in 2-to-10y maturities from August 2027 and keeps long-end sizes stable, with the ramp taking place over several quarters. Fed purchases of bills are expected to help absorb higher bill issuance.

Debt limit: absent preemptive action to raise it, Treasury's borrowing constraints may push bill issuance toward the back of the year. Treasury would work within the headroom from extraordinary measures and cash on hand until Congress raises or suspends the limit.

Euro Area net supply to the public is projected to fall from €1,059bn to €927bn in 2027. German supply rises (€232bn to €253bn) as fiscal support builds. EU net funding roughly halves as NGEU ends, and Spain is expected to stay fiscally conservative despite upcoming elections.

ECB QT is becoming friendlier because of the maturity profile of ECB holdings. GS sees risks skewed toward further QT deceleration, given excess liquidity moving into the plausible equilibrium range for bank reserve demand and the sovereign stress that emerged in the second half of 2026.

UK: net Gilt supply to the public should fall from £197bn to £163bn in 2027 as BoE QT slows and the DMO's shorter issuance mix reduces the duration risk investors must absorb. Greater bill reliance could add duration relief, though GS does not expect a substantial shift away from Gilts.

Japan: net supply to the public rises from ¥66tn to ¥70tn in 2027 on higher new JGB issuance from the MoF's budget request. BoJ QT stays about stable, so higher net issuance passes one-for-one into higher supply to the public. Funding increases are skewed to front-end and belly maturities.

Net supply to the public is about 5% of GDP in the US, Germany and the UK, and closer to 10% in Japan. Free float (debt outstanding ex-central bank holdings, as a share of GDP) should grow about 1-2pp in the US and UK, 4pp in Germany and 6-7pp in Japan.
Total US net issuance net of Fed holdings across Treasuries, agency MBS and USD IG should keep rising in notional terms on higher IG supply, but stay steady as a share of nominal GDP.
Swap spreads: GS leans constructive on US spreads (mainly carry) and UK spreads, and sees risks skewed toward tighter swap spreads in Germany and Japan.

US swap spreads: valuations are fair in the front end and on the wide side of fair value at longer maturities. Lower macro vol, Treasury's demand-sensitive issuance and better bank intermediation capacity support a tighter range and lower spread vol. GS frames spreads as carry rather than having much further to widen, with issuance risk likely later in the year after a debt limit resolution when bill supply and coupon sizes may rise.

Germany: GS expects renewed Bund cheapening versus swaps. Staggered relief in sovereign credit should reduce Bund safe-haven value and undo part of the year-to-date outperformance, and rising German free float adds cheapening pressure. A risk is that a balance sheet policy adjustment by the ECB would support Bund spreads.

UK: lower duration supply and a friendlier QT profile should offset the small headwind from rising free float, supporting modest further widening in 10y and 30y Gilt swap spreads. The fair-value model shows incremental valuation support at 10y, and 30y spreads screen roughly fair but are more sensitive to reduced duration supply.

Japan: JGB swap spreads have been supported by reduced long-end issuance and domestic demand optimism, and sit on the wide side of fair value. GS sees risks tilted to modestly tighter JGB swap spreads next year as free float grows.

risk_factors: Debt limit mechanics could backload US bill issuance, and the supply risk to US spreads may come after a debt limit resolution when Treasury ramps up bill supply to rebuild the TGA alongside coupon increases.
Euro sovereign stress and a further ECB QT slowdown or balance sheet policy adjustment could support Bund spreads, against GS's cheapening call.
UK longer-term fiscal challenges remain unresolved even as 2027 net Gilt supply falls.
Japan's net supply and free float increase faster than other G4 markets, with the long-end supply-demand balance managed by skewing issuance to the front end and belly.
JGB spreads could stay on the wide side of macro drivers longer than GS expects.
vol_and_positioning: US 10y UST-OIS swap spread volatility and trading range have been more subdued than last year. GS expects a lower vol macro baseline to help spreads sustain a tighter range.
US OIS-UST swap spreads are fair versus the model at the front end and wide of fair value at longer maturities (2y to 30y).
UK OIS-Gilt spreads: 10y has incremental valuation support and 30y screens broadly fair.
JGB swap spreads sit on the wide side of fair value.
geopolitical: Sovereign stress emerged in the euro area in the second half of 2026, which GS cites as a reason ECB QT may decelerate further and as a driver of Bund safe-haven value.
Spanish elections are upcoming, with GS expecting Spain to remain on a fiscally conservative path.

tension_points.bull_case: Prior to sovereign stress, 10y Bund spreads were comparatively stable in the face of increased supply. A larger ECB QT share of the free-float rise means a balance sheet policy adjustment would support Bund spreads.
tension_points.bear_case: Staggered relief in sovereign credit should reduce Bund safe-haven value and undo part of the year-to-date outperformance versus swaps. Rising German free float adds cheapening pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An ECB balance sheet policy adjustment, such as slowing or ending QT, would support Bund spreads and challenge the cheapening call.

theme_stances.evidence: stable or lower net supply to the public next year

theme_stances.evidence: we lean constructive on spreads in the US
